title: fix(plugin-auth)!: a password reset ends what the account added before it
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D1WDVL9JpCQhTUF97fpymtZ)_

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` teaches the reset, change, verification-link, magic-link, texted-code or API-key doors this narrows (a `git grep` of `skills/` for them answers nothing); the platform docs are updated here (`content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`)

## 维护者速读

- 用户在登录页用邮件或短信重置密码后：账号此前的 API 密钥被吊销、已关联的第三方登录被解除、已授权的应用（如 MCP 客户端）需要重新授权（以前都保留），管理员或运维人员强制重置密码时同样如此；正常修改密码不动它们，但会给账号邮箱发一封提醒，列出仍然有效的密钥、关联登录和已授权应用，已授权应用改密前拿到的访问令牌失效，需用刷新令牌换一个新的。
- 延续上一轮「改密即结束此前签发的访问」这一规则：账号第一次被设上密码（重置、管理员设置、邀请）也算一次改密，此前发出的自动登录验证链接、免密登录链接和短信登录验证码随之作废；注册时一并设下的密码不算，无论注册过程中的其他步骤耗时多久。
- 依赖旧 API 密钥的脚本、已授权的应用在账号重置密码（含管理员或运维人员强制重置）后会被拒，需要重新生成密钥（或在密钥列表里恢复）、重新授权应用，不会自动刷新令牌的 MCP 客户端在正常改密后也要重新连接一次；问题可直接撤回本次合并恢复原行为。
- 无

## What changes

A password reset ends what the account added before it, and a password change reminds the account what it keeps. One rule and one clock: everything here reads the credential clock that `readCredentialChangedAt` / `issuedBeforeCredentialChange` already provide.

**A completed self-service reset ends what the account added.** On success of `POST /reset-password` or `POST /phone-number/reset-password`, for the account the before-hook named, the global after-hook (`password-reset-ends-added-access.ts`) ends:

| What the account added | On this build | What the reset does |
|---|---|---|
| API keys (`sys_api_key`) | present | every key the admission seam would still admit on its flag (`revoked` false **or unset**) is written `revoked: true` (paged, a key read twice is an error, never a loop); no `revoked_reason`, the same as a key its owner revokes; the seam then answers it `403 API_KEY_REVOKED` |
| Linked sign-in accounts (`sys_account`, any provider other than `credential`: social, generic OAuth, SSO; `/link-social` is mounted) | present | deleted through better-auth's internal adapter, so its account-delete hooks run; the links are read again after the deletes, and one a host's `account.delete.before` kept is not counted as ended: the reset answers an error. No unlink record is written, so a provider links again as it did the first time |
| Authorized apps (`oauthConsent`, `oauthRefreshToken`, `oauthAccessToken` rows of the account) | present where the `oauth-provider` plugin is mounted: on by default, since it follows the MCP server | deleted, so each app asks to be authorized again and an MCP access token of the grant is refused on its next request; not read where the plugin is not mounted |
| Approved device sign-ins not yet collected (`deviceCode` rows of the account) | present where the `device-authorization` plugin is mounted (off by default) | deleted; not read where the plugin is not mounted |
| Passkeys | **not present**: the `passkeys` flag is wired to no plugin and no passkey store is mounted | nothing to end; named in the module header so a store mounted later joins the list |

A reset that does not complete ends nothing. A completed reset that cannot end one of these (a record it cannot read or write, a link a host hook keeps, or an account it cannot name because the before-hook's read of it failed) answers an error once the password is written; the next completed reset ends what is left. The password's change stamp and history entry (ADR-0069 D1) are written **before** that step, so a failed ending never leaves the written password without them.

**A password change keeps them and reminds.** `POST /change-password` ends none of these: an authorized app keeps its authorization (the MCP access token it held is refused, below, and its refresh token gets it a new one). When the account still holds, afterwards, an API key that is neither revoked nor past its own `expires_at`, a linked sign-in account, or an authorized app (named by its OAuth client's name, else its client id, read with one `in` read per page of client ids; listed only where `oauth-provider` is mounted), the account's address is sent the new built-in `auth.password_changed_notice` through the existing email service (`sendTemplate`, `identityMail`, no new transport), naming each. Keys and consents are read in pages, not one page of 500. Best-effort, like the email-change notice: it never fails the change. plugin-email ships it in en-US, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES (`BUILTIN_AUTH_TEMPLATES` 32 → 36 rows; variables `apiKeyCount`, `apiKeys`, `signInAccountCount`, `signInAccounts`, `authorizedAppCount`, `authorizedApps`), and core's `PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES_BY_TYPE.email_template` names it beside the other eight.

**Administrator and operator resets.** `POST /admin/set-user-password` with `revokeSessionsAndKeys` on (the default) and `os user set-password` already ended sessions and keys through `forced-reset-revocation.ts`; that module now also unlinks every non-credential sign-in account (`provider_id` filtered in the `where`), ends the apps authorized to the account and its approved device sign-ins, and revokes a key whose `revoked` flag is unset as well as one whose flag is false. The apps arm is the self-service reset's own (`endOAuthGrants`). The administrator's reset hands it better-auth's adapter and the same mount test as the self-service reset: the `oauthConsent`, `oauthRefreshToken` and `oauthAccessToken` rows of the account are deleted where `oauth-provider` is mounted, its `deviceCode` rows where `device-authorization` is mounted, and none is read where neither is. The operator's command runs with no server, so it has no plugin registry to ask; it hands the arm the project database (`storedOAuthGrants`), which deletes the account's `sys_oauth_consent`, `sys_oauth_refresh_token`, `sys_oauth_access_token` and `sys_device_code` rows the database holds (a table that is not there holds none). The response's `revoked` gains `signInAccounts` and `authorizedApps` (the consents ended), the ledger row gains `revokedSignInAccounts` and `revokedAuthorizedApps`, and the operator outcome gains `signInAccountsUnlinked` and `authorizedAppsEnded`. An arm that cannot finish counts in `revoked.failed` and leaves `complete` false, as the other arms do; the apps it ended before the failure are still counted, since the arm counts each row as it deletes it. An administrator who passes `revokeSessionsAndKeys: false` asks for a routine reset: that switch is the code's reason not to treat it as a self-service reset, and it still ends nothing. The one-step invitation door only ever sets the password of an account with no sign-in and no standing grant, so it has nothing of this to end.

**An account's first password, set onto an account that was already there, is a password change.** `readCredentialChangedAt` used to read a credential row not written over since its creation as "never changed". It now reads it so only when the row was created **in the same request as its account**, told by the request, not by elapsed time:
- `user.create.before` notes the address of the account the request creates on the request's endpoint context, and `account.create.before` gives a `credential` row created for that account in that request an id derived from the account's (`firstPasswordRowId`: `ACCOUNT_ID-credential`, never the account's own id, which names its `sys_user` row; `firstPasswordMark`, composed after the host's own hook in `auth-manager-database-hooks.ts`). A sign-up with a password, an administrator's create-user, the one-step door creating a new account: not a change, however long the hooks between the two creations take;
- every other credential row not written over is a change at its creation: either reset door creating the first password (`resetCredentialPassword` creates the row), `/admin/set-user-password`, the one-step door setting the first password of an existing account, `/set-initial-password`, and a row created outside a request better-auth serves.

A row written over is a change at its last write; "not written over" is bounded on both sides (an update stamp before the creation stamp reads as written over). A clock that cannot be read answers "issued before" (fail closed). The operator reset refuses an account with no local password, so it never creates a first one.

**An MCP access token issued before the account's password changed is refused.** The grant read the MCP door makes on every request (`mcpConsentAdmits`) now also reads the account's credential clock, the one that already ends links and codes (`readCredentialChangedAt`, through better-auth's internal adapter): a token whose `iat` falls before the account's last password write (a reset, a change, an administrator's `set-user-password`, `os user set-password`) is refused, whatever grant it was minted under. The comparison is `issuedBeforeCredentialChange` in whole seconds, as for a signed link, so a token minted in the second of the change is refused too. A reset ends the grant as well; a change, and an administrator's set with `revokeSessionsAndKeys: false`, keep it, so the app gets a new token with its refresh token, issued after the change. A clock that cannot be read refuses, and so does a grant read with no clock to read. The door makes one more indexed read per request: the account's password row.

**Links and codes that sign in follow the same clock.** The before-hook now ends, when minted before the account's credential change:
- a `/verify-email` token without `updateTo`, on a deployment with `emailVerification.autoSignInAfterVerification: true`. It answers what a never-issued token answers (`401 INVALID_TOKEN` or the `error=INVALID_TOKEN` redirect). With auto-sign-in off, the link signs nobody in and the vendor judges it as before;
- a magic link at `GET /magic-link/verify`. Its issue time is its `magic-link:TOKEN` verification row's creation. It answers the vendor's own never-issued redirect and opens no session. A non-plain `storeToken` or an unreadable row ends the link (fail closed);
- a texted sign-in code at `POST /phone-number/verify` (sent by `/phone-number/send-otp`). Its issue time is the earlier of its verification row's creation and its expiry less the plugin's code life (`expiresIn`, 300 s by default), so a wrong attempt that writes the row again does not date it after the change. It answers `400 OTP_NOT_FOUND` with no session, what a code never sent answers. A verify with `updatePhoneNumber` or `disableSession` signs nobody in and is judged by the vendor as before.

Links and codes minted after the change work as usual.

### Read first (by risk)

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts` `mcpConsentAdmits`: the credential clock read after the client and before the consent (so it binds every grant), the `iat` check moved ahead of it, and `!clock` refusing; `auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts` hands it better-auth's `internalAdapter`. Every MCP request runs this.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`: `readCredentialChangedAt` with `noteAccountCreatedInRequest` / `firstPasswordMark` (the first-password mark), and `accountBefore` in `auth-manager-database-hooks.ts`, which merges the host hook's data with the mark; then `endPhoneCodeIssuedBeforeCredentialChange` (the code's issue time).
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts` → `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts` and `forced-reset-revocation.ts`: the stamp and history block runs first; the reset branch throws when it cannot name the account; the OAuth arm runs only where its plugin is mounted and counts each row as it deletes it (`endOAuthGrants`, `endAuthorizedApps`); the key reads select a false or unset flag; the sign-in account arm's `provider_id` sits in the `where`; the admin route's mount test, and `storedOAuthGrants` (the operator's rows; a missing-table error answers none only when it names the table read).

## Tests

Every new case runs through the real routes: AuthManager + AuthPlugin on Hono over SQLite ObjectQL, the vendor's own endpoints, a captured mail and SMS service, and keys admitted through core's `resolveApiKeyAdmission`.

- `password-reset-ends-added-access.test.ts` (new, 22 cases): the emailed reset and the texted reset end every key (one with an unset flag included) and the github link (control: the new password signs in, a key minted after admits); a reset that does not complete ends nothing; a refused write answers ≥ 500; a failed ending still writes the stamp and the history entry (the replaced password is then refused as reused); a reset whose account cannot be named answers an error; a link a host `account.delete.before` keeps answers an error; with the OAuth provider and device authorization mounted, a reset ends the account's consents, refresh and access tokens and device codes, and an MCP token of the grant goes from admitted to refused, while another account keeps its own (control: unmounted, `oidcProvider: false`, nothing read or ended); an administrator's forced reset ends the same rows and reports `revoked.authorizedApps: 1` with `complete: true`, and the MCP token of the grant goes from admitted to refused, while with the switch off it ends none and the token stays admitted, and the administrator keeps their own grants; the operator's reset ends them as the project database holds them (`authorizedAppsEnded: 1`, `revocationComplete: true`), the administrator's kept; control: where neither plugin is mounted the administrator's forced reset reports `authorizedApps: 0`, `complete: true`, and every row stays; a forced reset whose refresh-token delete fails reports `authorizedApps: 1`, `failed: 1`, `complete: false` (the consent gone, the refresh token left); the MCP door's grant read refuses a token issued before a completed self-service reset, before an administrator's forced reset and before a password change, whatever its grant, and admits one issued a second after each (the controls), the change keeping the consent; with no clock to read it answers no and throws nothing; a change keeps them and its notice lists the app (`authorizedApps: 'Desk Assistant'`); a change keeps the key and the link and the notice lists them but not a revoked or an expired key; an account holding neither is sent nothing; admin with the switch off ends nothing, on gives the unset-flag key too; the operator reset gives `signInAccountsUnlinked: 1`.
- `credential-change-ends-prior-access.test.ts`: the clock's unit cases (a marked row is no change, an unmarked one is a change at its creation, an update stamp before the creation stamp is written over); a sign-up whose host `user.create.before` is held 1.2 s still creates the first password and the verification link it mails signs in; an administrator's create-user whose `user.create.after` is held 1.2 s the same; a sign-up-with-password control; the emailed reset, the texted reset and `/admin/set-user-password` each creating the first password end an email-change link minted before; a verification link with auto-sign-in (with the auto-sign-in-off control); a magic link (no session, never-issued redirect; one minted after signs in); a texted code sent before a password change answers `OTP_NOT_FOUND` with no session, what a code never sent answers (control: one sent after signs in), also after a wrong attempt with `disableSession` wrote it again.
- `auth-manager.mcp-oauth.test.ts`: the door refuses a token issued before its subject's password last changed whatever its grant, including one minted in the second of the change, and admits one from the second after (the control); an unreadable clock and no clock refuse (control: a readable one admits); a standing grant costs three reads, the client, the clock and the consent. Its store double, and `auth-manager.mcp-verifier-keyring.test.ts`'s, now answer the clock (no password row: never changed).
- `mcp-token-revocation.test.ts`: on the real provider, the tokens two apps hold, issued before a password change, are refused at the door whatever their grant, and the token each app refreshes into admits.
- `auth-manager.mcp-oauth-resource.test.ts`, `auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts`: their raw better-auth server writes the sign-up's password without the platform's first-password mark, which the clock reads as a password change, so their sign-up helper now waits for the next second before the app is issued its token, as a person's app would be.
- `admin-user-endpoints.test.ts`: the four exact `revoked` shapes gain `authorizedApps: 0` (the unit fakes mount no OAuth plugin), and the ledger row's closed decision set gains `revokedAuthorizedApps`; the dogfood ledger pin (`admin-ledger-decision-metadata.dogfood.test.ts`) lists it among the optional keys.
- `invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts`: the one-step door setting the first password of an existing account reads a change; one creating the account with it reads none.
- The nine auth test files this PR edits that reach main's SSO discovery egress guard (the five MCP door files this round among them) import `@objectstack/core/egress` at module top: the source under test reaches it through a dynamic import, and `check-test-source-alias` asks for its first load to be paid during collection.
- plugin-email: the notice in all four locales (subject, what stays active including authorized apps, the reset road, no "safe to ignore" footer, no en-US text in other locales) and its render pinned in `builtin-auth-render-identity.test.ts`.

## Acceptance notes

- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION** of a pending release note: `.changeset/credential-change-ends-prior-access.md` said "An account's first password is not a change." That sentence is now false for a first password set onto an existing account, so this PR deletes it; this PR's changeset states the new rule. `check-empty-changeset` is red on that file by design.
- A password reset revokes the account's keys **without** a `revoked_reason`, so the owner can restore one from the API Keys list, the same as a key the owner revoked. The administrator's forced reset keeps `admin_password_reset`, which only a platform administrator restores. Kept deliberately.
- A reset unlinks **every** non-credential sign-in account, including the one the account signed up with. Signing in with it again links it again when the provider's address matches (implicit linking writes no unlink record here).
- When the after-hook's ending fails after the password write, the reset answers an error although the new password is in place, with its stamp and history entry written. This is deliberate: an ending that does not happen must not read as success. The requester resets again.
- The OAuth provider is mounted by default (it follows the MCP server), so on a default deployment a reset, self-service or forced with revocation on, ends the account's MCP authorizations too; with `oidcProvider: false` the self-service and the administrator's resets read none of those stores.
- The operator's `os user set-password` runs with no server and cannot ask which plugins are mounted, so it ends the authorized-app and device sign-in rows the project database holds; a table that is not there holds none.
- A password change, and an administrator's routine set, now refuse the MCP access tokens issued before them. The authorization stands, so the app gets a new token with its refresh token, as it does when a token expires; an app that does not refresh on a `401` asks the person to connect again.
- A token issued in the same second as the password change, after it, is refused too (`iat` is whole seconds, as for a signed link); the app's next refresh, a second later, admits.
- The MCP door makes one more indexed read per request: the account's password row, through better-auth's `findCredentialAccount`.
- The change reminder leaves out revoked keys and keys past their own expiry. A key that admission refuses for inactivity or for the legacy grace may still be listed: those rules live inside core and are not exported.
- A credential row created before this release carries no mark, so it reads as a change at its creation. Only a link that signs in, or an MCP access token, minted before that row's creation (in practice, a sign-up's own link from before this release, in the same second) is affected; its owner requests a new one.
- The email-OTP reset (`/email-otp/reset-password`) is not wired on this build, so there is nothing for it.
